extracted.intended_audience: postsecondary institution administrators, Title IX coordinators, institutional decision-makers, and policymakers
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural criteria for conducting Title IX sexual harassment grievance processes at postsecondary institutions, with emphasis on live hearings, cross-examination, privacy, accommodations, and decision-maker duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-examination as part of a fair, truth-seeking grievance process
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department believes cross-examination is a necessary part of a fair, truth-seeking grievance process in postsecondary institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-examination provides value to both parties by allowing challenge of consistency, accuracy, memory, and credibility. The regulations include cross-examination while adding safeguards to minimize traumatic effects on complainants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Live hearing with parties in separate rooms upon request
rubrics_metrics.description: The entire live hearing (not only cross-examination) must occur with the parties in separate rooms, at the request of any party, with technology enabling participants to see and hear each other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This avoids face-to-face encounters and is intended to reduce trauma; recipients must facilitate technology to enable remote but real-time participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-examination conducted only by party advisors (never by a party personally)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cross-examination must never be conducted by a party personally; it must occur directly, orally, and in real-time by the party's advisor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rule prevents respondents from personally questioning complainants and is intended to maintain recipient neutrality and reduce retraumatization associated with direct confrontation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Only relevant cross-examination questions must be answered
rubrics_metrics.description: Only relevant cross-examination or other questions may be asked of a party or witness, and only relevant cross-examination questions must be answered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decision-makers must determine the relevance of each cross-examination question before the party or witness answers and must explain any decision to exclude a question as not relevant. This limits intrusive or irrelevant inquiry (e.g., most prior sexual behavior).

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision-maker determination and explanation of relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: The decision-maker must determine the relevance of a cross-examination question before a party or witness answers and explain any decision to exclude a question as not relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires active gatekeeping by decision-makers to ensure questioning stays focused on allegations; includes training expectations so decision-makers can make these determinations impartially.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients may adopt rules of decorum applied equally
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may adopt rules that govern the conduct and decorum of participants at live hearings so long as such rules comply with the regulations and apply equally to both parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions can prohibit abusive or disrespectful questioning and create hearing-specific decorum rules (e.g., limits on advisors) but must apply them symmetrically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision-maker training on live hearings and relevance (including prior sexual history)
rubrics_metrics.description: Decision-makers must be trained on conducting live hearings and determining relevance (including the non-relevance of questions and evidence about a complainant's prior sexual history).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training is required to ensure proper gatekeeping, protect privacy, and avoid erroneous credibility findings based on irrelevant matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disability accommodations and good-cause extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must comply with obligations under applicable disability laws; disability accommodations (e.g., short-term postponement for medical treatment for anxiety or depression) may be good cause for a limited extension of the grievance process time frame.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accommodations should be provided as needed to ensure participation and fairness; extensions for health needs are permissible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive measures available without filing a formal complaint
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must offer supportive measures to each complainant without waiting for a factual adjudication; complainants can receive supportive measures without filing a formal complaint or participating in the grievance process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This preserves complainant autonomy and provides non-traumatic options for reporting and obtaining interim relief regardless of whether a formal complaint is pursued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on access to treatment records and scope of exchanged evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must not access or use any party's treatment records without written consent, and evidence exchange is limited to evidence directly related to the allegations in the formal complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These provisions protect sensitive medical and counseling information and restrict the universe of evidence to what is directly relevant to the charged allegations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality and anti-retaliation protections (§106.71)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must keep party and witness identities confidential except as permitted by law and as needed to conduct an investigation, hearing, or judicial proceeding; retaliation is prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confidentiality obligations apply broadly to reporters, complainants, respondents, and witnesses to protect privacy and deter retaliation; disclosures are allowed only when necessary or legally required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety measures and remedies (no-contact orders, emergency removal, post-adjudication remedies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Safety-related measures remain available, including the ability to impose no-contact orders and to remove a respondent on an emergency basis; remedies are available when a respondent is found responsible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions should use interim and final remedies to protect access to education and safety while following procedural fairness requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients' discretion to educate community about cross-examination and oversee conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients retain discretion to educate their community about what cross-examination will look like and to develop rules and practices (applying equally) to oversee cross-examination to ensure questioning is relevant, respectful, and non-abusive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proactive community education and institution-specific rules can reduce fear, set expectations, and operationalize decorum and relevance enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients' obligation to investigate and evaluate all relevant evidence (burden to gather evidence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients are obligated to gather relevant evidence and objectively evaluate all relevant evidence, both inculpatory and exculpatory, including parties' statements and other evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-examination occurs at the end of the process after parties have had opportunity to inspect and review collected evidence; institutions must not rely solely on party statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: No right to self-representation in hearings; advisors as buffers
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulations do not grant a right of self-representation; party advisors (who need not be attorneys) conduct cross-examination and serve as buffers to prevent direct confrontation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This departs from criminal/civil courtroom norms to reduce trauma risk (e.g., prevents a respondent from personally cross-examining a complainant). Institutions may provide advisors and can require advisor compliance with decorum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-recorded testimony does not replace live hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: Allowing pre-recorded testimony in lieu of answering questions during a live hearing would not sufficiently accomplish the function of cross-examination in the postsecondary context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Live, real-time answers allow immediate follow-up to probe inconsistencies; pre-recording limits the ability to test testimony through follow-up questioning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient responsibility to prevent hearings from becoming 'kangaroo courts'
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients retain the ability and responsibility to ensure hearings function as truth-seeking processes rather than unregulated, abusive proceedings (e.g., control over abusive advisors, requirement that advisors comply with decorum, ability to replace advisors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions should enforce rules, require advisors to follow decorum, replace noncompliant advisors (including those provided by the institution), and ensure neutrality so non-lawyer advisors are not permitted to 'play attorney' in abusive ways.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit unreliability of demeanor-based credibility assessments
rubrics_metrics.description: Demeanor is the most unreliable factor in credibility assessments; decision-makers should be aware that assessments of facial expressions and body language are ambiguous and subject to bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decision-makers should place primary weight on specific detail, inherent plausibility, internal consistency, corroborative evidence, and not overvalue demeanor—recognize risks of misinterpretation, stress responses, and racial or other biases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal cross-examination rights for complainants and respondents
rubrics_metrics.description: An equal right of cross-examination for both parties is contemplated so that complainants' allegations and respondents' denials equally warrant probes for credibility and truthfulness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing symmetric cross-examination rights supports both parties' ability to advocate and aims to produce more accurate, balanced outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on irrelevant questions about prior sexual behavior or predisposition (with specified exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions and evidence regarding a complainant's prior sexual behavior or sexual predisposition are deemed irrelevant, with specified exceptions, and therefore generally disallowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decision-makers must be trained to identify and exclude such irrelevant evidence/questions unless a specified exception applies; this protects complainant privacy and focuses the hearing on allegations at issue.
